articles.title: Could psychedelics aid therapy for personality disorders? An unusual case offers a first look
articles.summary: A 37-year-old woman with severe personality disorders took psychedelics on her own during a year of therapy, despite her clinicians’ concerns. By the end, she no longer met criteria for two of her four diagnoses.

articles.title: Schizophrenia is linked to broad difficulty reading emotions from body language and faces
articles.summary: Reading emotions from body language and facial expressions helps people navigate social life. A study in Germany found that men with schizophrenia were less accurate at both, using displays in which faces and bodies were reduced to moving dots.

articles.summary: arXiv:2611.03662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects large language model agents to external tools and services through official SDKs that implement message validation and session logic. articles.title: Functional-Group Knowledge Is Structured in Language Models Before It Is Spoken
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.03684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models serve as the reasoning core of agents for chemistry and materials science, where they must interpret molecular structure before planning syntheses or proposing materials. Yet their outputs show only what they say, not what they know. Given a prompt such as ``The primary functional group in 1-Fluorobutane (CCCCF) is'', a small general-purpose model may answer ``the alkyne group'' instead of an alkyl fluoride. articles.title: Towards Automatic Heart Murmur Characterization from Multi-spot Phonocardiograms
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.03654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cardiac auscultation traditionally detects the presence of a heart murmur, but clinicians further characterize it by timing, shape, pitch, quality, and grade. Most automatic phonocardiogram analysis systems stop at binary detection and do not estimate this richer description. In this work, we formulate automatic murmur characterization as five patient-level classification tasks and compare three multi-spot strategies on recordings from the aortic, pulmonary, mitral, and tricuspid auscultation locations. articles.title: Socially isolated and lonely people tend to be biologically older than their years
articles.summary: Having no one to confide in was linked to an older biological age about as strongly as feeling lonely, according to a study of more than 300,000 adults that also tied isolation and loneliness to higher mortality.

articles.title: Brain structure carries clues about who prefers instant gratification, study suggests
articles.summary: Would you take $20 today or $50 next month? A new brain imaging study suggests the answer may be partly reflected in the volumes of brain regions tied to reward and long-term planning.

articles.title: House Republicans accuse the American Psychological Association of tolerating antisemitism
articles.summary: A House Republican report accuses the American Psychological Association of letting antisemitism fester and dismissing Jewish psychologists’ concerns, citing internal emails. The APA rejects the findings and says it unequivocally condemns antisemitism.

articles.title: Can watching sports make voters accept political defeats?
articles.summary: Watching athletes and coaches gracefully accept defeat in televised sports can make voters more accepting of political losses. New research shows that observing good sportsmanship directly increases the likelihood that voters will believe an unfavorable election was fair.

articles.title: Curriculum unlearning in humans and neural networks
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.04565v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: During learning, humans often benefit from curricula that teach simple rules before exceptions. However, we lack a computational explanation for this phenomenon. Here, using a canonical behavioural task and modelling with neural networks, we develop and test a theory for why simple-to-complex curricula succeed. We show that during learning, both humans and neural networks show simplicity biases, a tendency to learn simple rules that are underfit to the data. In neural networks this bias is accompanied by compression of neural representations. S

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? articles.title: Scientists discover new Alzheimer’s drug that repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can tackle several key features of Alzheimer’s disease, including DNA damage and inflammation. Already tested for initial safety in humans, the experimental treatment could offer a faster path toward therapies that target the disease at its roots.
